set.approach: From the Conrad Kain hut and Applebee campground, go up to the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col, then cross the Upper Vowell Glacier heading west to the foot of Pigeon Spire. Continue north past the spire to the highest point of the glacier then scramble up to the ridge crest from the south side, where the route begins. Expect glacier travel with crevasses and snow bridges, so carry rope and glacier gear.
set.descent_text: The usual way down is to reverse the ridge, downclimbing the easy fifth-class and fourth-class ground between the summits. Short rappels from the summit block and past the steeper sections are an option, and many parties simul-climb the ridge in both directions. At the low point of the ridge, descend the glacier and return over the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col to the hut.

review.notes: Approach via B/S col and Upper Vowell Glacier agreed by route page, area page and trip account; descent options (reverse ridge, optional short rappels) from route page and trip account; rappel counts differ so none given.

set.approach: The east face is plainly visible from the Bugaboo Glacier. Follow the climbers' trail west over loose rock to the Bugaboo Glacier, passing below the south side of Snowpatch Spire. Continue up the glacier, staying a little south of Pigeon Spire to avoid large crevasses, then traverse north above them and drop into a small bergschrund to reach the start of the route.
set.descent_text: The route finishes on the summit, and the West Ridge is the main descent from the summit for routes on the spire. Reverse that ridge, with short rappels as needed, to the low point, then descend the Upper Vowell Glacier side and return over the Bugaboo-Snowpatch col to the hut.

review.notes: Approach from route page, matching the area page's east/south face approach. Summit finish from route page; West Ridge as the spire's main descent from area page.

set.approach: Reach the south face by taking the Bugaboo Glacier west, passing below the south face of Snowpatch Spire. The route starts from the midway glacial bench a short way above the toe of the face, where two large west-facing corners stand side by side. Begin in the center of the right wall of the westernmost corner, just right of a prominent arch, on the right-most crack that gains the ridge soonest.
set.descent_text: From the top, scramble down the east ridge until a ledge system on the south side leads back to the last bolted belay. Every belay on the route is bolted for rappelling, so parties descend by rappelling the line. A long rappel from the top of the fifth pitch reaches the mid-way ledge.

review.notes: Descent and start location from the route page only; glacier approach to the south face from the area page.

set.approach: The traverse starts from the summit of South Illusion Peak, whose easiest line is a third-class ridge on its south side, reached from the col shared with North Nesakwatch. From the summit, drop slightly north to a viewpoint above the gap between the two peaks, where the rappel into the notch begins.
set.descent_text: The route ends on the summit of North Illusion Peak. To get off, reverse the traverse: scramble down the ridge toward the south until it forces a rappel onto the au cheval section, ride the au cheval to its north end, rappel into the notch, and climb the north ridge of South Illusion Peak to its summit. Then descend the third-class ridge on its south side to the col shared with North Nesakwatch.

review.notes: Start and finish from the S-N page; return from the N-S page; south ridge and col from the South Illusion area page.

set.approach: From the Phelix hut, follow the trail past the hut to the upper lake. Ford the outlet stream below the lake, then head straight up the boulder field toward the vertical face on the sub-peak, then continue left to the base of the steep gully where the route starts. The start can shift with snow cover at the base.
set.descent_text: The route tops out on the rim of the cliff, and parties walk off the top to the west side. The way back down can pass around the far side of the upper lake.

review.notes: Approach from both pages (area page gives hut-to-lake trail, route page the base); walk-off west from route page, lake loop from area page.

set.approach: Reach the northeast face by the Zeballos road and the Atluck Lake turnoff, then a logging spur above the south side of the lake, driving as far as the road allows. Continue on foot up the road to the fresh cutblock at its end, which comes close to the avalanche cone at the foot of the steep northeast faces. Cross the cutblock and a thin strip of trees to the approach slabs, then scramble easy slabs (third and fourth class) up to the foot of the wall and its snow patch. The start is in the corner, entered by way of the moat that opens in season along the patch's north edge.

review.notes: Approach from route page, road access confirmed by the area page. No top-out descent stated, so none written.

set.approach: The approach is the same as for the regular southwest face route. Take the trail that climbs along the old N20 logging road, follow the cleared path toward the face, and scramble the approach slabs up to the wide ledge below the first pitch. A ramp trending up and left marks the start; cairns at the base help locate it.
set.descent_text: The route tops out just below the point where the Walsh-Facer-Hutchinson route reaches the summit tower, and that route is the way down to Nathan Col. In a dry summer it can be followed without crossing snow. The belays on the route are bolted with rappel rings, which allows retreat down the line.

review.notes: Route page gives top-out and descent via the WFH route; approach from route and area pages and the first-ascent account (slabs, improved trail).

set.approach: The spire stands in Blackcomb Resort. Start at the Rendezvous Hut where the Blackcomb gondola ends, and pass the 7th Heaven chair and cross to the Horstman Glacier. From the upper end of the Showcase T-bar, turn north and follow the ridge crest; soon the spire appears straight ahead.
set.descent_text: The way off the spire is either an airy Tyrolean traverse across the chasm back to the ridge, or a more conventional rappel.

review.notes: Approach and both descent options from the area page; the Tyrolean back to the ridge is also in the magazine article.

set.approach: From the Kwoiek Creek forest road, follow North Kwoiek Road, which is overgrown, and ford the creek crossing it. Before the road forks, bushwhack up the fall line toward the ridge, using the gully with a creek. At treeline, contour around into the large alpine bowl with small lakes, then climb to the ridge crest and follow it west toward Winter Peak, where the scrambling begins.
set.descent_text: The route ends on the summit of Skihist Mountain, and the descent is the standard Skihist route down to the valley. Back at the overgrown lower section of the Kwoiek Creek road, either follow the road closely, which means crossing the creek twice without bridges, or bushwhack north of the three lakes to rejoin the road beyond the third lake.

review.notes: Approach agrees across route page and the first-ascent account; descent from route page only. No distances or current road status given.

bc_sahadeva_spire_friends_in_high_places.skip_reason: Fly-in route in the Arjuna group with no trail; the only descent report is a single account with a rappel count, which needs a second source.

bc_sawtooth_peak_the_fang.skip_reason: Page gives only the start from a col and a crack; no top-out descent, and no approach beyond that getting there is hard.
